records.title: Explorations in Human Centered Design
records.header: HCDE 210 Explorations in Human Centered Design (3) SSc
records.text: HCDE 210 Explorations in Human Centered Design (3) SSc Explores the core principles, methodologies, and applications of human centered design practice. Areas of investigation include user research, ideation, interaction design, visualization, prototyping, and usability. Cannot be taken for credit if credit has already been earned for HCDE 302.

records.title: Foundations of Human Centered Design I
records.header: HCDE 302 Foundations of Human Centered Design I (5)
records.text: HCDE 302 Foundations of Human Centered Design I (5) Explores the human-centered design paradigm from a broad perspective. Emphasizes the importance of developing and applying design processes and strategies. Students learn to think like a user-centered designer and carry out activities that are key to user-centered design.

records.title: Visual Communication in Human Centered Design and Engineering
records.header: HCDE 308 Visual Communication in Human Centered Design and Engineering (5) A&H
records.text: HCDE 308 Visual Communication in Human Centered Design and Engineering (5) A&H Introduces principles of visual communication and design used in human centered design and engineering so that students gain a systematic understanding as they create visual communication components of print, interactive, and video media. Students develop this understanding through hands-on exercises, design critiques, discussions, lectures, and readings in a studio environment.

records.title: Interactive Systems Design and Technology
records.header: HCDE 310 Interactive Systems Design and Technology (5)
records.text: HCDE 310 Interactive Systems Design and Technology (5) Provides opportunities to identify and build interactive systems to solve problems in human centered design and engineering. Students specify, design, build, and justify design solutions in terms of user experience and technical design choices. Prerequisite: either CSE 121, CSE 122, CSE 123, CSE 142, or CSE 160.

records.title: Introduction to User Research
records.text: HCDE 313 Introduction to User Research (5) Introduces user research methods, such as interviews, surveys, usability tests, content analysis, and focus groups. Reviews selecting an appropriate research method, how to conduct research and analyze results, conveying research data in the form of design requirements, and ethics.

records.title: Inclusive Design and Engineering
records.header: HCDE 315 Inclusive Design and Engineering (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: HCDE 315 Inclusive Design and Engineering (5) SSc, DIV Surveys a range of methods that examine, support, and interrogate design and engineering for disability and inclusivity. Students enact inclusive methods, reflect on their capacities to broaden design and engineering goals, and critique and evaluate their effectiveness from a variety of perspectives.

records.title: Sustainable Design
records.text: HCDE 316 Sustainable Design (5) Explores the environmental and societal impacts of digital products and services while mastering sustainable design principles. Introduces key concepts like lifecycle assessment and cradle-to-cradle design. Through hands-on projects, students build a sustainable design framework that applies to both physical and digital materials.

records.title: Professional Portfolio
records.text: HCDE 321 Professional Portfolio (2) Prepares students for professional practice by developing expertise and artifacts that make up an effective professional portfolio for careers in human centered design and engineering. Covers job searches, networking, recruiting, and interviewing, as well as development of resumes, cover letters, and online portfolios. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Organizational Teamwork
records.text: HCDE 322 Organizational Teamwork (2) Introduces students to teamwork and leadership competencies of particular significance to interdisciplinary, design-oriented, creative, and distributed work of human-centered design and engineering. Particular emphasis on competencies related to interpersonal interactions, group dynamics, and civic responsibility. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: User Experience Prototyping Techniques
records.text: HCDE 351 User Experience Prototyping Techniques (5) Introduces students to a variety of prototyping techniques for different kinds of user experience design problems. Structured as a series of independent explorations, each on a different prototyping methodology, aimed at many platforms. Prerequisite: either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303, which may be taken concurrently.

records.title: Human Data Interaction
records.text: HCDE 410 Human Data Interaction (5) Builds data science literacy anchored in the principles and methods of human centered design. Focuses on principles of data science and its human implications, including research ethics; data privacy; legal frameworks; algorithmic bias, transparency, fairness, and accountability; data provenance, curation, preservation, and reproducibility; user experience design and research for big data; human computation; and social impacts of data science. Prerequisite: either CSE 121, CSE 122, CSE 123, CSE 142, CSE 143, CSE 160, or CSE 163; either HCDE 210, HCDE 303, INFO 360, or both HCDE 300 and HCDE 318; and HCDE 310
records.prerequisiteText: either CSE 121, CSE 122, CSE 123, CSE 142, CSE 143, CSE 160, or CSE 163; either HCDE 210, HCDE 303, INFO 360, or both HCDE 300 and HCDE 318; and HCDE 310

records.title: Information Visualization
records.text: HCDE 411 Information Visualization (5) SSc/A&H Introduces the design and presentation of digital information. Covers the use of graphics, animation, sound, and other modalities in presenting information to the user; understanding vision and perception; methods of presenting complex information to enhance comprehension and analysis; and the incorporation of visualization techniques into human-computer interfaces. Course overlaps with: CSE 412; CSE 442; and STAT 451. Prerequisite: HCDE 310; and either HCDE 210, HCDE 303, INFO 360, or both HCDE 300 and HCDE 318.
records.prerequisiteText: HCDE 310; and either HCDE 210, HCDE 303, INFO 360, or both HCDE 300 and HCDE 318.

records.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Human Centered Design and Engineering
records.header: HCDE 412 Qualitative Research Methods in Human Centered Design and Engineering (5)
records.text: HCDE 412 Qualitative Research Methods in Human Centered Design and Engineering (5) Explores qualitative research methodologies, particularly the use of grounded theory methods to conduct field research for design and engineering. Develops skills for understanding and investigating why and how people experience, make meaning, and participate in their own social worlds, including how to create and iterate research questions, observations, and interviews. Course overlaps with: COM 383. Prerequisite: HCDE 313; and either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.
records.prerequisiteText: HCDE 313; and either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.

records.title: Usability Research Techniques
records.text: HCDE 417 Usability Research Techniques (5) Introduces usability research methods used in the product-development process; contextual inquiry, surveys and interviews, focus groups, user profiling, usability testing, cognitive walkthroughs, heuristics, and others. Prerequisite: HCDE 313; and either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.

records.title: Advanced Projects in Human Centered Design and Engineering
records.header: HCDE 418 Advanced Projects in Human Centered Design and Engineering (5, max. 10)
records.text: HCDE 418 Advanced Projects in Human Centered Design and Engineering (5, max. 10) Explores advanced topics in human centered design. Students engage with and discuss an advanced topic and then apply it by researching, designing, and implementing a solution to a design challenge. Team-based investigations culminate in a project response to the challenge. Prerequisite: either HCDE 303, INFO 360, CSE 440, or HCDE 300 and HCDE 318.
records.prerequisiteText: either HCDE 303, INFO 360, CSE 440, or HCDE 300 and HCDE 318.

records.title: Concepts in Human-Computer Interaction
records.header: HCDE 419 Concepts in Human-Computer Interaction (5) SSc
records.text: HCDE 419 Concepts in Human-Computer Interaction (5) SSc Studies the social, cognitive, behavioral, and contextual aspects of information systems and informational dimensions of the human-computer interface, and other user-centered design concepts. Surveys research literature of human information behavior, as well as ethical standards. Prerequisite: either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.
records.prerequisiteText: either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.

records.title: Web Technologies
records.text: HCDE 438 Web Technologies (5) Covers technical knowledge and skills related to web development including design issues, markup languages, client-side and server-side scripting, and data management technologies. Students learn to use these technologies at a core level of functionality, and leverage this knowledge either to manage others using these technologies or to expand and extend their abilities with these technologies Prerequisite: either HCDE 310 or CSE 160; and either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.

records.title: Physical Computing
records.text: HCDE 439 Physical Computing (5) Introduction to engineering and prototyping interactive systems and environments for human-centered applications that employ basic digital electronics components and circuits. Students build systems using micro-controllers and software tools. Provides hands-on experience in a project-based, studio environment. Prerequisite: HCDE 310; and either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.

records.title: Product Management
records.text: HCDE 450 Product Management (5) Introduction to product management. Students learn the broader organizational context within which they might work, helping them to better understand product development generally or as a preparatory step towards a career in product management. Covers key topics including strategic planning, effective communication, leadership skills, management principles, and the phases of the product development lifecycle. Prerequisite: either HCDE 300 and HCDE 318, or HCDE 303.

records.title: Material and Cultural Bias in Algorithmic Systems
records.header: HCDE 485 Material and Cultural Bias in Algorithmic Systems (5) A&H
records.text: HCDE 485 Material and Cultural Bias in Algorithmic Systems (5) A&H Project based course which examines the merging of data science, and arts and design practices. Draws from a range of theoretical texts and artistic works, combining textile and statistics literatures. Emphasizes mingling of ideas, multiple interpretations, and translations to critically represent, express, and challenge biased datasets and skewed machine learning systems. Offered: jointly with DXARTS 485.
